bull.t: Record IET orders and backlog visibility
bull.b: Record IET bookings, a 2.2x book-to-bill ratio, and record RPO provide substantial multi-year revenue visibility. This backlog supports planning and utilization across the installed equipment base, while strong order intake reinforces Baker Hughes’ position in LNG, gas infrastructure, and industrial energy markets.

bull.t: Improving margins and strong cash generation
bull.b: Higher adjusted EBITDA margins alongside robust free cash flow indicate improving operating execution and meaningful internal funding capacity. Sustained profitability can support investment, debt reduction, and aftermarket development, strengthening resilience across Baker Hughes’ equipment and service businesses over coming quarters.

bull.t: Chart acquisition broadens industrial and aftermarket exposure
bull.b: Chart expands Baker Hughes beyond traditional oilfield exposure into thermal management, industrial infrastructure, and carbon capture. Its technologies and aftermarket potential can diversify revenue, create cross-selling opportunities, and support longer-term margin and cash-generation improvement if integration milestones are achieved.

bear.t: Sharp weakness and volatility in reported revenue growth
bear.b: The sharply negative trailing revenue-growth figure raises concern about the consistency and timing of top-line expansion, even though margins remain solid. Uneven revenue conversion can make operating leverage harder to sustain and may limit the predictability of earnings across Baker Hughes’ cyclical markets.

The step-up in debt materially reduces financial flexibility relative to prior years and increases sensitivity to cyclical energy demand. Higher leverage can constrain capital allocation and leave less capacity for investment or shareholder returns, although management has stated an intention to deleverage within 24 months.

bear.t: Large IET orders may convert slowly into revenue
bear.b: Strong IET bookings do not translate immediately into sales because longer GTE cycles and aero-derivative supply-chain timing defer revenue conversion. This creates a near-term gap between order momentum and reported growth, potentially delaying the earnings and cash benefits of recent contract wins.
